output_json.patch_notes: Added a new private helper assertValidOutputPath(String outPath, File file) and a single call to it in getOutputStream immediately after the File is constructed (line 424), before file.getParentFile().mkdirs() and before the FileOutputStream is created. The helper resolves File(outPath).getCanonicalFile() and file.getCanonicalPath(), then rejects the entry unless the canonical file path equals the canonical output directory or starts with canonicalOutDir + File.separator. IOException from canonicalization is wrapped in ZipException. No public API, signatures, or existing behavior for legitimate entries changed; only entries that escape the target directory are now rejected with a clear ZipException.
output_json.risk_notes: Low risk. The change only adds a rejection path for entries whose resolved location falls outside the requested output directory; normal entries (including nested subdirectories within the target) still pass because they are descendants of the canonical output directory. Using canonical paths correctly handles ".." segments, redundant separators, and symlinks in the existing path prefix. The project has no existing test directory, so no unit tests could be added to the established structure without introducing new test infrastructure; compilation was verified via the Docker build wrapper (mvn -B -DskipTests package). The separately-run POV should now be blocked. Edge consideration: if a caller intentionally passed an entry name equal to the output dir itself, it is still permitted; traversal outside is blocked.
output_json.summary: Fixed a Zip Slip path traversal (CWE-022) in UnzipEngine.getOutputStream. During extraction the output file path was built by concatenating the caller's output directory with the archive entry name (fileHeader.getFileName()), which is fully attacker-controlled and may contain "../" sequences, allowing files to be written outside the intended extraction directory. Added assertValidOutputPath(), which canonicalizes both the target output directory and the resolved output file and throws a ZipException unless the file is contained within (equal to, or a descendant of) that directory. The check runs before any parent directories are created or the FileOutputStream is opened, so traversal attempts are blocked before any filesystem write occurs.
